HC-KAR  ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 08.03.2011 passed in MVC.No.243/2009 by the Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) &
MACT, Maddur, (for short, 'Tribunal').

2. Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of the learned counsel for the parties,
it is taken up for final disposal.

3. Sri.Vasanthapp, learned counsel for the appellants submits that the wife, children and mother of late H.Narayana filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short,
'M.V.Act').

Later, they filed a memo to treat the said petition under Section 163A of the MV Act,
which was allowed by the judgment and award dated 23.10.2010 passed in MVC No.243/2009 and compensation of Rs.3,69,500/- was awarded with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of NC: 2026:KHC:13240 HC-KAR petition till realization within 30 days.

It is further submitted that the insurance company has filed a review petition seeking review of the aforesaid judgment and award dated 23.10.2010 and the said review petition was allowed under the impugned judgment.

It is also submitted that the Tribunal has erred in allowing the review petition without appreciating the fact that there is no error apparent on the face of the record to review the judgment dated 23.10.2010.
It is contented that the claimants are even entitled to the compensation under the package policy to the extent of Rs.2,00,000/-.
Hence, he seeks to consider the same by allowing the appeal.

4. Per contra, Smt.Mamatha S.Shankar, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 - insurance company supports the impugned judgment and submits that the Tribunal has appreciated the error committed by it and reviewed its judgment, which does not call for any interference.

It is further submitted that the deceased was a driver and not the owner of the vehicle and due to his NC:
2026:KHC:13240 HC-KAR negligence the accident has caused, hence he is not entitled for any compensation.
Hence, she seeks to dismiss the appeal.
5. I have heard the arguments of the learned counsel appearing on both the sides and meticulously perused the material available on record.

6. The material on record indicate that one Sri.H.Narayana, died in a road accident that occurred on 09.11.2009 and the wife, children and mother of deceased H.Narayana filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V.Act before the Tribunal.

The Tribunal considered the rival submissions and after allowing the memo filed by the claimants, treated the said petition as the one filed under Section 163A of the M.V.Act and proceeded to award compensation Rs.3,69,500/- with the interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

The records indicate that respondent No.2 Smt. M. Kavitha vs Sri.H.Ramachandra on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158829615/
3 - insurance company filed a review petition under Order XLVII Rule 1 read with Section 114 of CPC seeking to NC: 2026:KHC:13240 HC-KAR review the judgment and award dated 23.10.2010 passed in MVC No.243/2009, which came to be allowed by the Tribunal under the impugned judgment.

entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: 7. The perusal of the judgment clearly indicates that the deceased was a driver and due to his negligence the accident is caused and he has died in the said accident.

Taking note of the said aspect and considering the decision of this Court reported in 2010 KAR MAC 466 KAR held that no other vehicle was involved in the accident and therefore, the deceased was not entitled for compensation and proceeded to award Rs.50,000/- as a compensation under Section 140 of the M.V.Act.
8.

The evidence on record clearly indicate that the accident is caused due to the fault of the deceased driver and by appreciating the said aspect, the Tribunal awarded Rs.50,000/- with interest with the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation of the amount within 30 days by exercising Section 140 of the M.V.Act.
NC: 2026:KHC:13240 HC-KAR
The claim for package policy or compulsory personal accident cover (CPA) cannot be considered as the deceased was the driver and the accident is caused due to his own negligence.
I do not find any error or perversity in the findings recorded by the Tribunal calling for interference in this appeal.
The appeal is devoid of merit and accordingly, same is rejected.
